prompt: Why can the planner compare `"2026-10-19" < "2026-10-24"` as strings?
hint: Look at the order of the parts.

choices.text: JavaScript converts both to dates before comparing
choices.why: It compares them as text, character by character.

choices.text: Year, month, day, zero-padded: text order is date order
choices.why: Right, which is why the format was chosen.

choices.text: Svelte's compiler rewrites string comparisons on dates
choices.why: `week.js` is a plain module; the compiler does not touch it.

choices.text: It only works here because both of those dates happen to fall in the same month
choices.why: It works across months and years too, for the same reason.

prompt: `week.js` does every calculation in UTC. What goes wrong without that?
hint: A date at midnight in one zone is the day before in another.

choices.text: Nothing; time zones only matter for times, not dates
choices.why: A date parsed at local midnight can print as the previous day.

choices.text: The planner would refuse to load on a computer set to a time zone other than Brazil's
choices.why: Nothing refuses; the dates would quietly shift.

choices.text: A date comes out a day early on a computer in the Americas
choices.why: Right. The same input gives the same answer everywhere only if the zone is fixed.

prompt: Session 6 is on Saturday 24 October 2026. `mondayOf` returns the Monday of its week. Which day of October is that?
hint: Count back from Saturday.

prompt: Why are `planner.json` and `week.js` plain files with no runes in them?
hint: Where do runes belong?

choices.text: Nothing in them changes while the page is open
choices.why: Right: runes go where values change, and these can be tested on their own.

choices.text: Runes are forbidden in any file under `src/lib`
choices.why: `src/lib` holds components with runes, like `WeekTotal.svelte`.

choices.text: JSON and JavaScript files cannot be imported by a component
choices.why: The page imports both.

choices.text: They would be faster with runes, but runes are still experimental
choices.why: Runes are Svelte 5's normal syntax, and speed is not the reason.

prompt: How does the `Next week` button change the week shown?
hint: Read its handler.

choices.text: It calls a setter function that `$state` returned
choices.why: `$state` returns the value itself; there is no setter.

choices.text: It assigns a new value to `week`
choices.why: Right. The compiler turned that assignment into a signal write.

choices.text: It reloads the page with the next week in the address
choices.why: Nothing reloads; `look` stayed at `/`.

choices.text: It sends the new week to the development server
choices.why: The state lives in the browser; the server is not asked.

prompt: `let week = $state(mondayOf(data.sessions.at(-1).date))`. How many times does `mondayOf` run while you click the week buttons?
hint: When is the initial value computed?

choices.text: Once per click, to recompute the starting week
choices.why: The declaration is not re-run; clicks only assign to `week`.

choices.text: Twice per click: once before the change and once again after it
choices.why: Nothing calls it on a click at all.

choices.text: Once, when the component is created; clicks do not call it
choices.why: Right. The initial value is computed once.

prompt: Which of these should NOT be its own `$state`?
hint: Could you work it out from the others?

choices.text: The week being shown
choices.why: Nothing else determines it; the buttons set it.

choices.text: The label `Week of 19 Oct 2026`
choices.why: Right. It is computed from `week`, so storing it twice invites the two to disagree.

choices.text: Which course the student selected
choices.why: Only a click can tell you that, so it is state.

choices.text: The list of sessions, once sessions can be added
choices.why: Additions cannot be worked out from anything else.

prompt: If you deleted a variable and could work its value out from the others, it is ___, not state.
hint: The next rune.

prompt: `Previous week` only sets `week`. Why does the total change too?
hint: Follow the chain in the figure.

choices.text: `total` is derived from `thisWeek`, which is derived from `week`
choices.why: Right. Each link recalculates when next read.

choices.text: The handler also recalculates the total, hidden by the compiler
choices.why: The compiler adds no recalculation to handlers; the derived values do it themselves.

choices.text: The whole component re-runs when any state changes
choices.why: That is React's model; the script ran once.

choices.text: The browser recomputes every expression in braces on each click
choices.why: Only the expressions whose signals changed run again.

prompt: Match each property of a derived value with what it means.
hint: Three properties, three meanings.

pairs.right: Recalculated when next read, not when marked out of date
Read ten times, calculated once until something changes
Computes a value and does nothing else

right_distractors: Recalculated on a timer, every animation frame

prompt: When do you write `$derived.by(() => …)` rather than `$derived(…)`?
hint: Compare `total` and `byCourse`.

choices.text: When the value is an object rather than a number
choices.why: The type of the result does not matter; the shape of the computation does.

choices.text: When the calculation is slow and should run in the background
choices.why: Both forms run in the same place, at the same time.

choices.text: When computing it takes several statements
choices.why: Right. `.by` takes a function body; the plain form takes one expression.

choices.text: When it depends on more than one piece of state
choices.why: A one-expression derived can read any number of signals.

prompt: `{minutesFor(course)}` in the markup and `{byCourse[course.id]}` show the same number. What differs?
hint: How often does each one compute?

choices.text: The function version is not reactive, so it stops updating after the first time it runs
choices.why: A call in the markup is tracked: it reads state, so it re-runs.

choices.text: The call runs each time its markup updates; the derived value runs once per change and is shared
choices.why: Right. Both are correct; the derived value is cheaper and has a name.

choices.text: The derived value is computed on the server only
choices.why: It is computed wherever the component runs, browser included.

prompt: `sessions.push({...})` on a `$state` array. What updates?
hint: The proxy reports writes.

choices.text: Nothing; you have to assign a new array to `sessions`
choices.why: That is needed with `$state.raw`, not with deep state.

choices.text: Everything that read the array, such as the totals and the list
choices.why: Right. The proxy saw the push.

choices.text: Only the `{#each}` that walks the array; derived values keep their old results
choices.why: The derived values read the array too, so they are out of date as well.

choices.text: The page reloads with the new session
choices.why: Nothing reloads.

prompt: Marking a session done printed no `update` from `$inspect(total)`. Why?
hint: What does `total` read from each session?

choices.text: `$inspect` only reports pushes, not property changes
choices.why: It reports any change to what it tracks; `total` simply did not change.

choices.text: Toggle buttons do not change state
choices.why: This one assigned `session.done`, and the button showed `[pressed]`.

choices.text: `total` reads `minutes`, not `done`
choices.why: Right. The write reached the button, which read `done`.

choices.text: The proxy ignores booleans to save memory
choices.why: Booleans are tracked like any property.

prompt: Why does the page keep the selected course as an id rather than as the course object?
hint: What does `$state` do to an object?

choices.text: Ids take less memory than objects
choices.why: True but beside the point; the trouble is comparing.

choices.text: A proxied object is not `===` the original, and a string compares cleanly
choices.why: Right. Comparing ids sidesteps the question.

choices.text: Objects cannot be passed to `aria-pressed`
choices.why: `aria-pressed` receives the result of a comparison, a boolean.

choices.text: Courses change while the page is open, and a stored object would go out of date with them
choices.why: They do not; the course list is a plain import.

prompt: Match each tool with when you reach for it.
hint: Two are runes, one is a method of a rune.

pairs.right: A large list you only ever replace whole
A plain copy, to log or send somewhere

right_distractors: A value shared between two browser tabs

prompt: You keep a `Date` object in `$state` and call `date.setDate(25)` on it. What happens on the page?
hint: Which objects does the proxy wrap?

choices.text: The date updates everywhere it is shown
choices.why: Only arrays and plain objects are proxied; a `Date` is left alone.

choices.text: An error: classes are not allowed in `$state`
choices.why: They are allowed; they are just not made deeply reactive.

choices.text: Nothing visible changes, because the change is not seen
choices.why: Right. Assign a new `Date`, or use `SvelteDate` from `svelte/reactivity`.

prompt: What is `$effect` for?
hint: Think about where its code reaches.

choices.text: Computing values from other values
choices.why: That is `$derived`.

choices.text: Responding to a click or a keypress
choices.why: That is an event handler.

choices.text: Reaching outside the component after the page updates
choices.why: Right: a title, a timer, a canvas, a connection.

choices.text: Running code on the server before the HTML is sent
choices.why: Effects never run during server rendering.

prompt: An effect starts a `setInterval` and returns nothing. It re-runs three times. How many intervals are running?
hint: Nothing stopped the earlier ones.

choices.text: One; Svelte stops the old interval for you
choices.why: Svelte calls the function you return, and here there is none.

choices.text: Four
choices.why: Right: the first run and three re-runs, none cleared. Return `() => clearInterval(id)`.

choices.text: Three, since the first run does not count
choices.why: The first run started one too.

choices.text: None; intervals are not allowed in effects
choices.why: They are allowed, and a timer is the usual example.

prompt: A teammate writes `$effect(() => { total = sum(thisWeek); })`. What do you suggest?
hint: It computes a value.

choices.text: `let total = $derived(sum(thisWeek))`
choices.why: Right. A value from other values is derived, computed when read, with no second update.

choices.text: Wrap the assignment in `untrack` so it cannot loop
choices.why: That hides one symptom and keeps the extra update and the stale moment.

choices.text: Use `$effect.pre` so it runs before the page updates
choices.why: Still an effect computing a value, which is the wrong tool.

choices.text: Move the line into the button's click handler
choices.why: Then the total would only follow one button, not every change to the sessions.

prompt: An effect that keeps setting a value it reads is stopped with the error `effect_update_depth____`.
hint: How deep the updates went.

prompt: `let { minutes, label = 'this week' } = $props();` and the parent writes `<WeekTotal minutes={total} />`. What is `label`?
hint: The parent passed one prop.

choices.text: `undefined`
choices.why: The default applies when the parent passes nothing.

choices.text: `'this week'`
choices.why: Right: the default.

choices.text: An error, because every prop must be passed
choices.why: A prop with a default is optional.

choices.text: The name of the parent component, as a fallback
choices.why: Svelte supplies no such fallback; the destructuring default does.

prompt: Inside `WeekTotal`, what happens if it assigns `minutes = 0`?
hint: Who owns the value?

choices.text: The parent's `total` becomes 0 too
choices.why: Props flow down; the parent's state is not touched.

choices.text: The child shows 0 until the parent passes a new value, which overwrites it
choices.why: Right. A child reads its props; changing the parent's value is lesson 5.

choices.text: Nothing; props are constants and the line is ignored
choices.why: The assignment works locally, which is exactly why it is a trap.

prompt: Match each way of writing props with what it does.
hint: One collects, one passes on, one is shorthand.

pairs.right: Passes them on to an element

right_distractors: Makes the prop writable by the child

prompt: The parent's `total` changes. Why does `WeekTotal`'s `hours` follow it?
hint: A prop is read like anything else.

choices.text: The child's script runs again with the new prop
choices.why: Scripts run once, children included.

choices.text: The parent recreates the child component from scratch whenever any of its props changes
choices.why: The child stays; only what read the prop updates.

choices.text: `hours` is derived from `minutes`, and reading a prop is tracked
choices.why: Right. Props are reactive reads like state.

prompt: Put the lesson's steps in the order the planner page was built.
hint: Each step needed the one before it.
items: `sessions` as deep state, with a push and a toggle
An effect for the document's title
trap: The total could not be derived before there was a week to derive it from.

prompt: Which of these belong in `$derived` rather than `$effect`? Choose all that apply.
hint: Does the code compute a value, or reach outside?

choices.text: The number of sessions done this week
choices.why: Yes: a value from other values.

choices.text: The sessions of the selected course, sorted by date
choices.why: Yes: still a value.

choices.text: Saving the sessions to `localStorage` when they change
choices.why: No: that reaches outside, so it is an effect.

choices.text: Setting `document.title`
choices.why: No: an effect, as the lesson did.
